## Safety contract

The preview and apply paths must share the exact same selector implementation. Preview returns the prospective immutable acknowledgement coordinates, counts, omissions, and recovery/apply command but writes no item, workspace, or history state. Apply records normal provenance and remains auditable.

## Empty-selection contract

Zero actionable coordinates is a successful, truthful no-op unless the caller selected a strict mode that explicitly makes no-match an error. The output must distinguish no match from malformed input, tracker corruption, and already-acknowledged coordinates.

## Scope

This is specific to history-author-acknowledge. It complements the broader update-many preview work but does not depend on it and must not be folded into a generic destructive-command rewrite.

patch.value:
## Selector and preview contract

CLI, SDK, and MCP preserve the existing exclusive selector grammar: repeated item-id:line event coordinates or all_actionable. The dry-run path and apply path use one SDK-native resolver. Preview returns selection.kind, canonical ordering by item_id then positive line, selected_count, omitted_count, a budget-bounded coordinates projection, and plan_fingerprint. The fingerprint is computed over the complete ordered coordinate set and the immutable source event hashes, so omitted coordinate rows do not weaken reproducibility.

## Apply-transition contract

Apply must consume the preview fingerprint instead of trusting a second unconstrained all_actionable evaluation: CLI --plan-fingerprint, SDK planFingerprint, and MCP plan_fingerprint name the same field. Apply re-resolves under the same selector, compares the complete fingerprint, and returns CONFLICT exit 4 with a fresh-preview recovery if any actionable coordinate or source event changed. No acknowledgement is written on mismatch.

## Outcome and exit contract

Zero matches and an explicit selection whose coordinates are all already acknowledged return outcome no_effect, acknowledged 0, mutated false, and exit 6. A mixed explicit selection with both newly actionable and already-acknowledged coordinates returns partial_effect and exit 7 with exact per-coordinate disposition rows. Malformed selectors return USAGE exit 2. Tracker or history corruption returns GENERIC_FAILURE exit 1. These stable outcomes replace the earlier unspecified strict-mode branch.

## Scope

This is specific to history-author-acknowledge. It complements the broader update-many preview work but does not depend on it and must not be folded into a generic destructive-command rewrite.

Bulk acknowledgement first returns a deterministic preview plan over item-id:line coordinates or all_actionable. Apply consumes that exact plan fingerprint and rejects selection drift. Zero actionable coordinates produce the standard no_effect outcome rather than a validation failure.

Add one SDK-native selector/plan primitive used by CLI and MCP; preserve the existing exclusive selector grammar of repeated --event item-id:line coordinates or --all-actionable; expose --dry-run and return selection.kind, deterministic item_id then line ordering, selected_count, omitted_count, bounded coordinates, and a stable plan_fingerprint computed over the complete ordered coordinate set plus source event hashes; require apply to provide CLI --plan-fingerprint, SDK planFingerprint, or MCP plan_fingerprint and reject any re-resolved fingerprint mismatch with CONFLICT exit 4 before mutation; use the existing effect-aware exits with zero matches or an all-already-acknowledged selection returning outcome no_effect and exit 6, a mixed actionable/already-acknowledged explicit selection returning partial_effect and exit 7, malformed selectors returning USAGE exit 2, and tracker/history corruption returning GENERIC_FAILURE exit 1; keep CLI, SDK action, MCP, contracts, completions, docs, and tests in parity; add unit, integration, acceptance, selection-drift, and disposable-directory manual proof.

The irreversible history-author-acknowledge --all-actionable path can mutate every actionable item-id:line coordinate without a preview plan. When the selector matches zero actionable coordinates it emits a misleading validation-style diagnostic instead of the effect-aware no_effect result, making recovery unsafe to plan and hard to automate.
